data.name: IXPN Lagos
data.notes:
The Layer 2 IXP was established in 2006. The Internet Exchange Point of Nigeria (IXPN) is known for a  neutral and not-for-profit organization focusing at facilitating the exchange of internet traffic among the ISPs and other network operators in Nigeria.  The IXPN is a key player in the global Internet ecosystem and a hub for many other important networks in Africa. By allowing ISPs and other networks to exchange traffic, IXPN helps to reduce costs and improve the efficiency of the internet in Nigeria. It enhances the possibilities the internet is accessible to all Nigerians, regardless of their geographic location.

The primary goal of IXPN is to reduce the cost and complexity of Internet traffic exchange in Nigeria, by allowing ISPs to directly interconnect their networks and exchange traffic locally, instead of routing traffic through international gateways. The infrastructure assists to make Internet access more affordable for everyone, regardless of their financial situation. This can increase access to educational materials and other resources that can bridge the information gap.

IXPN provides a range of services and infrastructure to support Internet traffic exchange, including physical infrastructure such as data centers, routers, and switches, as well as virtual infrastructure such as route servers and peering databases. It also provides technical assistance and training to its members to ensure that they can effectively utilize the IXPN infrastructure and services.

Today, IXPN is the largest and most active Internet Exchange Point in West Africa, with over 120 members, including ISPs, content providers, and telecommunications companies. Our system is instrumental in enhancing the quality and accessibility of Internet services in Nigeria, while also serving as a crucial hub for Internet traffic exchange throughout the region.

data.name: AR-IX Cabase - Argentina
data.notes:
Cabase is an internet exchange that includes facilities in several cities in Argentina.

Our main network is **switched inside a city** and **routed between cities**, to keep Layer2 problems local. Each city has its own route servers.

There is also a nationwide Layer2 VLAN that bridges all connected facilities, to be used as a private peering over our public IPs, without route servers.

We also provide VLANs between peers, when the public Layer2 VLAN can't be used and peers need a private exchange over their own IPs.

data.name: ERA-IX Amsterdam
data.notes:
A new era of peering!

The future of peering on internet exchanges is under pressure, due to ever-growing costs, high number of failures, and a "too corporate" culture. In mid-2022 two internet pioneers decided to bring a better and more cost-effective alternative, and we never looked back.

### Our mission
It is our mission to redefine peering, by offering an innovative and cost-effective IXP ecosystem. The current state of peering is not-so-great and in a headlock by large corporate IXP-operators.

### Our way
We are truly neutral, fully privately owned and funded. Powered by a new generation of internet pioneers, our goal is to offer transparent and enterprise-ready connectivity services with a human touch.

### About us
We are the new-generation connectivity partner, fully privately owned and funded. We have built a next-generation connectivity fabric across major datacenters in Amsterdam and Frankfurt. [Read more](https://www.eranium.io/about) about our initiative.

BGP Large Community Policy – Route Server AS154034

The route server (RS) recognizes and acts on the following large-community values.

General syntax:
154034:<action-code>:<peer-ASN>
Replace <peer-ASN> with the destination ASN (examples below use 65500 as a placeholder).

0 | Global Reject | Any prefix that carries 154034:0:0 is rejected. ---> 154034:0:0

0 | Per-Peer Reject | A prefix that carries 154034:0:<peer> is rejected only when exported to that specific peer ASN. ---> 154034:0:<Peer-AS>

1 | Announce a route to a certain peer | Allow the prefix to be advertised to a designated peer. ---> 154034:1:<Peer-AS>

101 | Prepend x1 | The RS prepends ASN 154034 once to the AS-PATH before sending the route to the peer. ---> 154034:101:<Peer-AS>

102	| Prepend x2 | The RS prepends ASN 154034 twice to the AS-PATH. ---> 154034:102:<Peer-AS>

103	| Prepend x3 | The RS prepends ASN 154034 three times to the AS-PATH. ---> 154034:103:<Peer-AS>

data.name: 3AM Network IX
data.notes:
3AM Network is a small open-peering internet exchange at Qupra DC, Amsterdam (AS202301). Peering LAN: `91.213.211.64/26` and `2001:7f8:17d::/64`. 

Most Amsterdam IXPs aren't really set up for networks that run BGP from a single VM - port-speed floors, sign-up calls, that sort of thing. 3AM is what happens when a few of those networks build their own. If you have an ASN and a way to reach Amsterdam, you're in: home labs, students learning BGP, hobby
ASNs, small commercial shops. Larger networks are welcome too; we just won't pretend to replace the big ones.

RS filtering: RPKI-required, IRR-based prefix lists, bogon and length sanity. No member fee, no setup fee.

To join: email **noc(at)3am.network** with your ASN and your IRR as-set and we will send you ways to cross-connects. We'll usually reply within a day.
